## Practice Final ##

For each of the following questions, please provide a short answer of not more than a few paragraphs (and maybe less if you don't need that much). The goal is to demonstrate your understanding of the ideas in question, not to explain every technical detail.

Answer on a document of your own, referencing each question as you answer it. Please do your own work. The exam is open-book and open-notes, but using any language copied directly from any source without attribution (including the internet or an AI) will be regarded as an academic integrity issue.

If you find that there is ambiguity in a question, please know that it is not a trick and not intentional. Adopt a reading that could resolve the ambiguity, explain your decision, and proceed.

####################
## Question 1     ##
####################

Many political scientists are interested in learning whether electoral rules (e.g., majority-rule voting vs. proportional representation) affect the size of the welfare state. The idea is that different kinds of electoral rules might push the middle class to usually ally with poor and working class voters, on the one hand, or with wealthy voters, on the other, with predictable consequences for welfare policy.

In this framework, what is the independent variable? What is the dependent variable? Is there a hypothesis about the causal pathway? If so, what?
